readings.title: 村庄之旅
readings.text: Last summer we took a short trip to a small village in the north. The distance from the city is about sixty miles, and the road crosses an old bridge over a wide river. We stopped at a farm to rest and bought fresh bread from the owner. In the afternoon we walked in the forest behind the village. The ground was soft and the air was cool. There were animals everywhere, and the place felt very safe and quiet. The whole tour took five hours, but nobody was tired. Before we left, the owner told us about an outdoor market on Sunday. I want to go back in winter, because the season changes everything here. My favorite part was the last hour, when the light went down behind the trees and the whole village became quiet. We took many photos, and I still look at them when I need a rest from the city.

readings.title: 在医院
readings.text: My father went to the hospital last month. The doctor asked about the pain in his back and took some blood for a test. The patient in the next bed was much older and had a different disease. The doctor said the problem was not serious, and he gave my father a drug to take twice a day with food. He also said regular exercise would help. There was no operation, and that was a great relief for all of us. The medicine cost very little, and the nurses were kind. Two weeks later the pain was gone. My father now walks for thirty minutes every morning. He says a small injury or a small pain is a warning from your body, and you should listen to it before it becomes significant. He also eats more vegetables and drinks more water. The doctor told him to come back in six months for a check.

readings.title: 我们的星球
readings.text: The earth is the only planet we can live on. Most of it is ocean, and the water is very deep in some places. On the land we have large forests, and every plant and animal there is part of one system. But we produce too much waste, and the damage is now easy to see: dirty rivers, dead trees and plastic in the sea. This is a worldwide problem, not a local one. The good news is that simple habits help. We can use less water, keep the ground clean, and protect the wild animals near our towns. My teacher says the earth does not need saving; we need saving from ourselves. In our town we now clean the river twice a year, and the water is much better. Every small action has an impact, and together they are significant. The habits themselves are not difficult; they only need to be regular.

readings.title: 选择职业
readings.text: Last year I had to make a difficult choice about my career. A large company offered me a job in another city, and I had to consider it carefully. The pay was good, but the work was not developing the skills I wanted. My manager said it was a great chance and that I should apply for the senior role later. In the end I said no. It was a hard decision, because the money was significant for my family. But I believed the new role would give me more responsibility and a better future. Six months later the same company called me again with a better opportunity. I took the interview and got the job. Sometimes waiting is the best strategy. I also learned that a career is not a straight road. You can say no, wait, and still arrive at the right place, as long as you know what you want to develop.

readings.title: 提高英语
readings.text: Many students ask me how to improve their English. The answer is simply time and habit, not talent. Read something in English every day, even a short text, and try to understand the new words from the sentence around them. Keep a small notebook for useful expressions, because native speakers use the same phrases again and again. Listen to the language on your way to work, and repeat what you hear out loud. A short session every day is better than one long lesson at the weekend. Do not worry about mistakes; they are part of real communication. If you want to master a foreign language, you must be patient. Your progress will feel slow, but one day you will notice that you are thinking in English without trying. Find a reason that matters to you: a job, a person, or a film you want to understand without subtitles. That reason will keep you going on the days when study feels heavy.

readings.title: 城市生活
readings.text: The population of our city has grown fast in ten years. New blocks were built in the northern part, and the roads are now full of traffic every morning. Public transport is cheap, but it is crowded at eight. The biggest problem is housing: the rent for a small flat is now higher than a monthly salary. Young people often share a flat with three or four others. On the good side, the city has excellent facilities: a large library, a modern sports hall and a swimming pool. Most people here come from other places, so the city feels open and modern. It is noisy and expensive, but it also gives you chances that a small town cannot. Most young people I know still want to stay, because the city gives them work and freedom. A small town is quieter, but it cannot offer the same future.

readings.title: 电子设备
readings.text: Every electronic device in my home has a screen, and I look at them for too many hours a day. My computer monitor is large, which is good for work, but my eyes are tired in the evening. The battery on my phone never lasts a whole day now, so I carry a small power pack. A good internet connection is necessary for almost everything I do, from paying bills to talking to my parents. The useful side is clear: I can work from home two days a week. The bad side is that I check messages during dinner. Last month I made a rule: no operations on any device after nine at night. It was difficult for one week, and then it became normal. I also turned off most message alerts, and that single change saved me almost an hour a day. In the evenings I read a book instead, and my sleep is much better.

readings.title: 乘飞机旅行
readings.text: Our flight to the capital leaves at six in the morning, so we must be at the airport two hours early. I reserve the seats online and pay for the ticket with a card, because they charge extra at the desk. I always keep my travel documents in one small bag: passport, ticket and the address of our hotel. The schedule says we arrive before noon, and our destination is only twenty minutes from the airport by transport. Flying is fast, but the waiting is the hard part. I take a book, some water and a little food, because the prices inside the airport are high. Last year our plane was three hours late, and that was simply part of travelling. Now I always plan one extra day. The worst part of any journey is the queue at security, so I wear simple shoes and keep my bag light. Little things like that make travelling much easier.

readings.text: At the start of every month my wife and I write down our budget. Our income comes from two sources: my job and her small shop. We then list what is necessary: rent, food, transport and the children's school costs. After that we see what is left. We try to spend less on things we do not need, and we cook at home instead of eating out four times a week. Last year we had a lot of debt, and that was a hard time for us. Now we keep a small amount of funds for emergencies, on a monthly basis. It is not exciting, but it works. The impact on our life is large: we sleep better and we argue less about money. We also write down every large purchase before we make it, and then we wait two days. Most of the time we do not buy it in the end.

readings.title: 外出就餐
readings.text: There is a small restaurant near the station that I visit every Friday. The owner is a friendly woman, and her kitchen is small but very clean. The menu changes with the season, which I like, because the food is always fresh. I usually ask what she recommended that day, and I have never been disappointed. Her fish is excellent, and the coffee is the best in this part of the city. The selected wines are cheap and good. Once she gave me the recipe for her soup, and I tried it at home, but it did not taste the same. I think good food is not only about the recipe; it is also about the person who cooks it and the place where you eat it. The restaurant is not expensive either, and that is another reason I go back every week. Good food does not have to cost a lot of money.

readings.title: 周末运动
readings.text: I play football with a small local team every Saturday. There are eleven players in the team, and we train twice a week in the evening. Our coach is a former player, and he says that regular exercise is better than hard exercise once a month. Last weekend the match was very close. The final score was two one, and we did not win, but nobody was angry. One of our players had a small injury and had to rest for two weeks. Since then we all do warm-up exercises before every session. Sport gives me more than strength; it gives me friends and a reason to go outdoor even in the coldest months. That is why I keep playing, year after year. Before every match we now go for a short run together, and that has made the team much stronger. Next season we want to enter a bigger competition.

readings.title: 冬日节日
readings.text: Every year in winter our town holds a small festival. The entire main street is closed to cars for three days, and the locations for music and food are set up in the square. My parents come to stay with us, and we also invite one guest from abroad. It is my favorite time of the year, even though the weather is cold. People sell hot drinks and warm clothing, and children run everywhere. On the last night there is a short race around the square, and the winner gets a small award. The festival is not large or famous, but it brings the whole town together. When the lights go out on the final evening, everyone feels a little sad, and we start waiting for the next season. My father says a town without a festival is a town without a memory. I think he is right.
